title: Orthodontic Benefit Riders Recovery Computation — Takeover Benefit Payable to Date and the Member's Repayment
content:
**Orthodontic Benefit Riders: what a takeover makes payable to date, and what the member repays.**

## Amounts read from the records

- **Amount paid on the case.** Every initial and installment payment carrying the case number, less every reversal carrying it.
- **Case benefit.** The allowed case fee less any unused part of the rider's lifetime orthodontic deductible, times the rider coinsurance for the network status on the establishment entry, rounded half up to the cent. It is limited to the person's remaining lifetime maximum on the establishment date. The payments already made on a case do not count against the benefit of a takeover entry that supersedes that case's new-start entry.
- **Takeover proration.** For a takeover case, the benefit so computed is prorated by the months remaining divided by the planned treatment months on its takeover entry, rounded half up to the cent, and is paid in installments only, with no initial payment. A takeover entry that supersedes a new-start entry of the same case is not prorated, because its fee already covers only the treatment from the start of coverage.
- **Deductible not yet used.** This is:
  - the whole deductible, when every establishment entry under the rider carries the case's case number;
  - the deductible less the allowed case fees on the establishment entries of the other cases, when those add up to less than the deductible;
  - nothing, otherwise.

## The takeover benefit and its installments

1. **Takeover benefit.** The allowed case fee on the latest establishment entry, less the part of the deductible not yet used, times the rider coinsurance for the network status on that entry, rounded half up to the cent. It is prorated as the takeover proration above states, and limited to the rider's lifetime maximum less the payments, net of reversals, made under the rider for other cases.
2. **Number of installments.** The takeover benefit is spread over the installments of the original schedule. That number is the planned treatment months after the banding month, limited to the rider's installment months cap, divided by the service-period length (one month, or three on a quarterly schedule), rounded up, and never fewer than one. Each takeover installment is the takeover benefit divided by that number, rounded half up to the cent.
3. **Service periods.** The takeover schedule keeps the original schedule's service periods. These start the rider's first-installment offset months after the banding month and follow one service period apart.
4. **First takeover installment.** It covers the service period in which coverage of the case began. When coverage began before the first service period of the original schedule, it covers that first service period instead, in full. Coverage of the case began in the month reached by counting forward from the banding month a number of months equal to the planned treatment months, less the months remaining on the takeover entry, plus one.
5. **Payable to date.** A takeover installment is payable to date once the first day of its service period has passed, and every payable installment is paid in full. No more takeover installments are payable to date than the number the takeover benefit is spread over.
6. **Repayment.** The member repays the amount paid on the case less the takeover installments payable to date, never below zero and never more than the initial payment of the case.

## Order of assembly

The repayment is assembled in one fixed order:

1. The fee comes down by every amount taken off it before coinsurance.
2. The takeover benefit is set and limited as stated.
3. Every amount taken off the takeover benefit comes off next.
4. Every percentage held back comes off the rest.
5. The remainder is divided into takeover installments, rounded half up to the cent.
6. The installments payable to date are added up, with every part-period share applied, and rounded half up to the cent.
7. The repayment is the amount paid on the case less that total, never below zero, never more than the initial payment, and rounded half up to the cent.

## Which case

- The case is the one whose establishment entries are the latest under the rider. When two entries carry the same date, the one entered first counts as the latest.
- A rider with no establishment entry has nothing to repay.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The case:

- a takeover entry superseding a new-start entry, with a recognised fee of 3,800.00, in network;
- hypothetical coinsurance of 50 percent and no deductible;
- 24 planned months and 19 months remaining;
- a monthly schedule with service periods starting 1 month after the banding month and a 24-month cap;
- amount paid on the case 1,300.00, of which the initial payment was 1,050.00;
- today is the 3rd day of the 9th month after the banding month.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Takeover benefit (not prorated) | 3,800.00 times 50 percent is 1,900.00 |
| Installments of the original schedule | 23 months after the banding month give 23 installments; 1,900.00 divided by 23 is 82.61 |
| Month coverage began | 24 less 19, plus 1, is the 6th month after the banding month |
| Installments payable to date | service periods of months 6, 7, 8 and 9, which is 4 installments totalling 330.44 |
| Repayment | 1,300.00 less 330.44 is 969.56, which is under the initial payment of 1,050.00 |
